--- title: "Module 0: Preliminary content" ---
![](../../src/images/hex_complex.png){.intro_image} Start here! These preliminary lessons contain the core knowledge and skills that I believe an early beginner in R should have obtained. The lessons also contain elements of the language that are often overlooked by those with considerable R experience. Even if you’re coming in with *loads* of R experience, you’ll almost certainly learn a thing or two along the way! - **[Preliminary Lesson 1: R & RStudio](0.1_intro_to_r_and_rstudio.qmd){target="_blank"}**: Install and set up R and RStudio, adjust RStudio's global options for a comfortable and reproducible workflow, and get oriented in the four core RStudio panes (Source, Console, Environment, and Output). - **[Preliminary Lesson 2: Environment & Functions](0.2_environment_and_functions.qmd){target="_blank"}**: Learn how R's environment tracks the objects you create, how assignment and functions work, when quotation marks are (and aren't) necessary, how to install and load packages, and best practices for commenting and naming your code. - **[Preliminary Lesson 3: Values](0.3_values.qmd){target="_blank"}**: Get to know the four atomic vector types you'll use throughout these lessons -- numeric (double and integer), character, factor, and logical -- and the common pitfalls that come with each. - **[Preliminary Lesson 4: Objects](0.4_objects.qmd){target="_blank"}**: Explore how atomic vectors, matrices, lists, and data frames differ in dimensions and homogeneity, how to construct and describe each, and how to read and write data with the *readr* package. - **[Preliminary Lesson 5: Indexing](0.5_indexing.qmd){target="_blank"}**: Learn to subset atomic vectors, matrices, lists, and data frames by position, name, or logical condition using `[...]`, `[[...]]`, `pluck()`, `$`, and the tidyverse's `filter()`. If you want additional practice we recommend the Swirl package, and have provided some guidance for that work here: . Those who consider themselves beginners in R should plan to do these lessons as well as those above. ## Reference ::: panel - **Arguments**: A value supplied to a function that modifies its behavior when the function runs. - **Assignment (noun)**: A reference that R uses to call data from your computer’s memory (also called "name"). - **Assignment (verb)**: The act of associating a name with an object (typically to the global environment). - **Assignment operator**: A function used to assign an object to a name. - **Atomic vector**: A one-dimensional, homogeneous data object (a set of values of the same class). - **Attributes**: Information about the values of an object that is not contained in the values themselves. - **Character**: A symbol or set of symbols from a given alphabet (note: also includes numbers and punctuation). - **Class**: A blueprint that describes an object's structure. - **Console pane**: A pane of RStudio used for interactively running R commands and viewing their output. - **Data frame**: A two-dimensional, heterogeneous data object comprised of equal-length vectors (a restrictive type of list under-the-hood). - **Dimensions**: The arrangement of values in an object; may also refer to the number of values or child objects within a given dimension (i.e., rows or columns) - **Double numeric vector**: An atomic numeric vector where the values are stored as decimal numbers (essentially). - **Environment**: A dimensionless data structure that contains references (names) to data stored in memory. - **Escape character**: A backslash (`\`) placed before a character to tell R to treat that character literally rather than as part of R's syntax. - **Factor**: A value that maps character labels onto integers. - **Filtering**: The process of subsetting a data frame's rows by a logical condition, most often with `filter()`. - **Function**: A set of instructions (stored as an R object) used to complete a given task. - **Global environment**: A workspace that provides a reference point for all user-assigned objects associated with the current session. - **Heterogeneous object**: A container that holds values of one or more object classes. - **Homogeneity**: Whether an object may contain one or more than one class of object. - **Homogeneous object**: a container that holds values of only one class. - **Index**: The location of a value or component object within a parent object. This term can also be used as a verb to describe the process of indexing. - **Indexing**: The process of subsetting an object by the position (location) of a value or component within it. - **Integer**: A whole number, or an atomic vector of data stored as whole numbers. - **Labels**: Character values supplied to the labels argument of factor() to rename the levels as a factor is created. - **Levels**: The character values mapped to a factor's integer values. - **Library**: The location of a package on your computer. - **List**: A one-dimensional, heterogeneous data object that can hold values or objects of any class. - **Logical constant**: `TRUE` or `FALSE`. - **Logical operator**: An operator used to test a logical statement (e.g., `3 > 2`). - **Matrix**: A two-dimensional, homogeneous data object arranged into rows and columns (an atomic vector under-the-hood). - **Metapackage**: A package that is comprised of more than one smaller packages. - **Name**: A symbol that R evaluates to retrieve the object associated with it through a binding in an environment. - **Nested function**: A function that is run inside of another function. - **Object**: A collection of one or more values or functions. - **One-dimensional object**: Objects where data are arranged in a single line. - **Operator**: A function expressed that is expressed as a symbol and is not followed by parentheses. - **Package**: A set of pre-written functions that can be downloaded (*note: There are also data packages!*) - **R session**: A running R process and its current state. - **Recursive object**: An object made up of references to other, nested objects (e.g., a list). - **Script**: A text file that contains a set of commands to read, manipulate, and analyze data. - **Session history**: All lines of code that have been sent to R since the beginning of a session (or since the session history was last cleared). - **Source pane**: A pane of RStudio used for writing, editing, and running scripts. - **String**: A character value comprised of more than one symbol. - **Structure**: The dimensionality, homogeneity, and storage class of a data object (may also describe its metadata). - **Subsetting**: Reduce a data object to a component or components of interest. - **Tibble**: A type of data frame with additional properties that make it especially useful. - **Two-dimensional object**: An object where data are arranged as rows and columns. - **Type**: How an object is stored in your computer. - **Vector**: A one-dimensional object. - **Viewer pane**: A pane of RStudio used for navigating your system's files, viewing help files, and images/plot output (and more) - **Workspace pane**: A pane of RStudio used to view/manage objects in your global environment and your session history. ::: ::: panel **Important!** Primitive functions, as well as functions in the packages that R attaches by default (e.g., *base*, *utils*, *stats*, and *graphics*), are available as soon as you start an R session. ::: function_table ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
